1.english_meaning: Everything available in our environment that can be used to satisfy our needs, provided it is technologically accessible, economically feasible, and culturally acceptable.
1.hindi_meaning: संसाधन - पर्यावरण में उपलब्ध प्रत्येक वस्तु जो हमारी आवश्यकताओं को पूरा कर सकती है, बशर्ते वह तकनीकी रूप से सुलभ, आर्थिक रूप से संभव और सांस्कृतिक रूप से मान्य हो।
1.example: Water, soil, and forests are important natural resources.

1.english_meaning: In a way that relates to technology or uses advanced tools and methods.
1.hindi_meaning: तकनीकी रूप से - तकनीक से संबंधित या वैज्ञानिक ज्ञान और उपकरणों का उपयोग करते हुए।
1.example: The area is not technologically advanced enough to extract deep underground minerals.

1.english_meaning: Able to be reached, used, or obtained easily.
1.hindi_meaning: सुलभ / पहुँच योग्य - जिस तक आसानी से पहुँचा जा सके या जिसका उपयोग किया जा सके।
1.example: Electricity should be easily accessible to all remote villages.

1.english_meaning: Possible to do easily or conveniently, especially from a financial perspective.
1.hindi_meaning: आर्थिक रूप से संभव / व्यावहारिक - जिसे आसानी से या लाभ के साथ पूरा किया जा सके।
1.example: Building a bridge over the deep valley was not economically feasible.

1.english_meaning: A thorough or dramatic change in form or appearance.
1.hindi_meaning: रूपांतरण - किसी चीज़ के रूप, स्वरूप या स्थिति में पूर्ण परिवर्तन।
1.example: The transformation of raw materials into finished goods requires industrial units.

1.english_meaning: Acting upon or influencing each other mutually.
1.hindi_meaning: अंतःक्रियात्मक / पारस्परिक प्रभाव डालने वाला - जहाँ दो या दो से अधिक तत्व एक-दूसरे को प्रभावित करते हैं।
1.example: There is an interactive relationship between human society and the natural environment.

1.english_meaning: To begin to move faster, or to cause something to happen sooner or at a faster rate.
1.hindi_meaning: गति देना / तीव्र करना - किसी प्रक्रिया या विकास को तेज करना।
1.example: Good infrastructure helps to accelerate economic development in a country.

1.english_meaning: A part or element of a larger whole, especially of a machine or system.
1.hindi_meaning: घटक / अंग - किसी बड़ी प्रणाली या व्यवस्था के आवश्यक भाग।
1.example: Human beings are essential components of resource creation.

1.english_meaning: Arranged in classes or categories according to shared qualities or characteristics.
1.hindi_meaning: वर्गीकृत - गुणों या विशेषताओं के आधार पर समूहों में बाँटा गया।
1.example: Resources can be classified on the basis of their origin and exhaustibility.

1.english_meaning: Relating to or resulting from living organisms.
1.hindi_meaning: जैविक - जीवित जीवों (पौधों और जानवरों) से संबंधित या प्राप्त।
1.example: Forests, fisheries, and wildlife are examples of biotic resources.

1.english_meaning: Relating to or resulting from non-living environmental factors.
1.hindi_meaning: अजैविक - निर्जीव वस्तुओं या तत्वों से संबंधित।
1.example: Rocks and metals are classified as abiotic resources.

1.english_meaning: The quality of being able to be used up completely or exhausted over time.
1.hindi_meaning: समाप्यता / खत्म होने की क्षमता - किसी संसाधन के उपयोग के बाद समाप्त होने का गुण।
1.example: Coal and petroleum are studied under the basis of exhaustibility.

1.english_meaning: Capable of being renewed, replenished, or restored naturally over time.
1.hindi_meaning: नवीकरणीय - जो प्राकृतिक रूप से थोड़े समय में पुनः पूरित या उत्पन्न हो सकें।
1.example: Solar and wind energy are abundant renewable resources.

1.english_meaning: Dependent on each other; mutually dependent.
1.hindi_meaning: परस्पर निर्भर - जब दो या दो से अधिक चीजें एक-दूसरे पर निर्भर करती हैं।
1.example: Nature, technology, and institutions have an interdependent relationship.

1.english_meaning: Having or showing the capacity to develop into something in the future.
1.hindi_meaning: संभावित - जिसमें भविष्य में उपयोग किए जाने की क्षमता हो लेकिन अभी पूरी तरह विकसित न हुआ हो।
1.example: Rajasthan has enormous potential for the development of wind and solar energy.

2.english_meaning: Stock or supply of materials, money, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively.
2.example: Water, forests, and minerals are essential natural resources.

2.english_meaning: In a way that does not show careful choice or planning, often resulting in harm.
2.example: Natural resources should not be used indiscriminately.

2.english_meaning: The reduction in the number or quantity of something, such as resources.
2.example: The depletion of fossil fuels is a major global concern.

2.english_meaning: The acquisition or gradual gathering of something.
2.example: The accumulation of wealth in a few hands leads to inequality.

2.english_meaning: The action or fact of treating someone or something unfairly in order to benefit from it.
2.example: Excessive exploitation of forests harms the environment.

2.english_meaning: The condition or process of degrading or being degraded, especially of the environment.

2.example: An equitable distribution of resources ensures social justice.

2.english_meaning: Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level without depleting natural resources.
2.example: We need to adopt sustainable practices to protect our planet.

2.english_meaning: Accept standards that are lower than is desirable, or harm something.
2.example: We must not compromise the needs of future generations.

2.english_meaning: Come or bring together for a meeting or activity; assembled.
2.example: World leaders convened in Rio de Janeiro for the Earth Summit.

2.english_meaning: Declare one's public approval or support of something.
2.example: The conference endorsed the global Forest Principles.

2.english_meaning: A formal or explicit statement or announcement.
2.example: The leaders signed a joint declaration on climate change.

2.english_meaning: Take action to reduce, destroy, or prevent something bad or undesirable.
2.example: Agenda 21 aims to combat environmental damage and poverty.

2.english_meaning: Having, showing, or done with good judgement or sense.
2.example: Resource planning ensures the judicious use of available minerals.

2.english_meaning: Very large in size or quantity; immense.
2.example: India has an enormous diversity in the availability of resources.

3.english_meaning: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively.
3.hindi_meaning: संसाधन - कोई भी वस्तु जिसका उपयोग आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए किया जा सके।
3.example: Water is a vital resource for all living beings.

3.english_meaning: Relating to the basic physical and organizational structures and facilities needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.
3.hindi_meaning: बुनियादी ढांचे से संबंधित - सड़क, बिजली, परिवहन जैसी मूलभूत सुविधाओं से जुड़ा।
3.example: Arunachal Pradesh lacks adequate infrastructural development.

3.english_meaning: Provided or equipped with a quality, ability, or asset.
3.hindi_meaning: संपन्न - प्राकृतिक रूप से किसी गुण या वस्तु से युक्त होना।
3.example: Rajasthan is well endowed with solar and wind energy.

3.english_meaning: Not having enough of a specified quality or ingredient.
3.hindi_meaning: अभावग्रस्त - किसी चीज़ की कमी होना।
3.example: The cold desert of Ladakh is deficient in water resources.

3.english_meaning: Provide resistance, delay, or obstruction to something or someone, making situation more difficult.
3.hindi_meaning: बाधा डालना - किसी कार्य में रुकावट पैदा करना।
3.example: Poor technology and lack of institutions may hinder development.

3.english_meaning: The action or process of settling among and establishing control over the indigenous people of an area.
3.hindi_meaning: उपनिवेशवाद - किसी शक्तिशाली देश द्वारा अन्य क्षेत्रों पर अधिकार करना और उनका शोषण करना।
3.example: The history of colonisation reveals that rich resources in colonies attracted foreign invaders.

3.english_meaning: Make full use of and derive benefit from a resource, often selfishly or unfairly.
3.hindi_meaning: शोषण करना या दोहन करना - संसाधनों का पूरा उपयोग या दुरुपयोग करना।
3.example: Foreign invaders used advanced technology to exploit resources of other regions.

3.english_meaning: The state or condition of being superior to all others in authority, power, or status.
3.hindi_meaning: सर्वोच्चता या प्रभुत्व - सबसे अधिक शक्ति या अधिकार होना।
3.example: Colonising countries established their supremacy over the colonies.

3.english_meaning: The action of conserving something, especially prevent loss, waste, or harm of natural resources.
3.hindi_meaning: संरक्षण - संसाधनों की बर्बादी को रोकना और उनका विवेकपूर्ण उपयोग करना।
3.example: Resource conservation is crucial for sustainable development.

3.english_meaning: Not logical or reasonable; lacking clear and sensible thinking.
3.hindi_meaning: अविवेकपूर्ण - बिना किसी तर्क या समझदारी के किया गया कार्य।
3.example: Irrational consumption of water leads to severe shortages.

3.english_meaning: The act of using something to excess or beyond sustainable limits.
3.hindi_meaning: अति-उपयोग - किसी चीज़ का जरूरत से ज्यादा इस्तेमाल करना।
3.example: Over-utilisation of fossil fuels causes environmental problems.

3.english_meaning: A complete list of items such as property, goods in stock, or the contents of a building.
3.hindi_meaning: सूची तैयार करना - किसी क्षेत्र में उपलब्ध संसाधनों का आकलन और सूची बनाना।
3.example: Resource planning involves the identification and inventory of resources across the country.

3.english_meaning: A rough calculation of the value, number, quantity, or extent of something.
3.hindi_meaning: आकलन - किसी मात्रा या मूल्य का अनुमान लगाना।
3.example: Quantitative estimation of minerals is a part of resource planning.

3.english_meaning: Jointly arranged, planned, or carried out; coordinated.
3.hindi_meaning: समन्वित या संयुक्त - मिलकर और योजनाबद्ध तरीके से किया गया प्रयास।
3.example: India has made concerted efforts for achieving the goals of resource planning.

3.english_meaning: Relating to a large and important organization, such as a university, bank, or church, or established laws and systems.
3.hindi_meaning: संस्थागत - संस्थाओं, नियमों और प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था से संबंधित।
3.example: Resource development requires appropriate technological and institutional changes.

4.english_meaning: The physical features of an area of land, such as mountains, plateaus, and plains.
4.example: India has land under a variety of relief features, namely mountains, plateaus, and plains.

4.english_meaning: Lasting or existing for a long or apparently infinite time; continuously flowing.
4.example: Himalayan rivers ensure the perennial flow of water throughout the year.

4.english_meaning: Relating to the relations of organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings.
4.example: Forests and mountains are vital for maintaining ecological balance.

4.english_meaning: A supply of a commodity not needed for immediate use but available for future use.
4.example: The plateau region possesses rich reserves of minerals and fossil fuels.

4.english_meaning: Farmland that is left unsown for a period in order to recover its fertility.
4.example: Current fallow land is left without cultivation for one or less than one agricultural year.

4.english_meaning: The arrangement of the natural and artificial physical features of an area.
4.example: The use of land is determined by physical factors such as topography and climate.

4.english_meaning: Making use of a situation or person unfairly for one's own advantage.
4.example: The exploitative nature of modern technology is a major cause of resource depletion.

4.english_meaning: Reduction in the number or quantity of something, such as natural resources.
4.example: Overuse of fossil fuels leads to the rapid depletion of natural resources.

4.english_meaning: Strongly influencing later developments; very important and original.
4.example: The Brundtland Commission made a seminal contribution to resource conservation.

4.english_meaning: Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level without depleting natural resources.
4.example: Sustainable development meets the needs of the present without compromising future generations.

4.english_meaning: The protection of plants, animals, and natural resources to prevent exploitation and destruction.
4.example: Resource conservation is essential for the survival of life on Earth.

4.english_meaning: Having limits or bounds; not infinite.
4.example: Land is an asset of a finite magnitude, so it must be used carefully.

4.english_meaning: Capable of being cultivated or farmed.
4.example: Culturable waste land has been left uncultivated for more than five agricultural years.

4.english_meaning: The great size, extent, or importance of something.
4.example: We must understand the magnitude of environmental problems we are facing today.

4.english_meaning: Publicly recommended or supported a particular cause or policy.
4.example: The report advocated resource conservation as a means to protect the environment.

5.english_meaning: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively.
5.hindi_meaning: संसाधन (वे सभी साधन जिनका उपयोग आवश्यकताएँ पूरी करने के लिए किया जाता है)
5.example: Water and land are vital natural resources for human survival.

5.english_meaning: Relating to geological features or the physical characteristics of a region.
5.example: The total geographical area of India is 3.28 million square kilometres.

5.english_meaning: To examine and record the features of an area of land to construct a map or plan.
5.hindi_meaning: सर्वेक्षण किया गया (भूमि का माप-जोख या अध्ययन करना)
5.example: Some areas of Jammu and Kashmir have not been surveyed yet.

5.english_meaning: Prepared and used for growing crops.
5.hindi_meaning: कृषि योग्य बनाया गया / जोता गया
5.example: These lands are cultivated once or twice in about two to three years.

5.english_meaning: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred.
5.example: The percentage of net sown area in India is about 54 per cent.

5.english_meaning: A part, share, or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.
5.example: Find out reasons for the low proportion of net sown area in these states.

5.english_meaning: Relating to ecology or the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings.
5.example: Forest cover is considered essential for the maintenance of the ecological balance.

5.english_meaning: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.
5.example: Trees play an important role in the maintenance of environmental quality.

5.english_meaning: A means of securing the necessities of life.
5.hindi_meaning: आजीविका (रोज़गार या जीवन चलाने का साधन)
5.example: The livelihood of millions of people depends on forests.

5.english_meaning: A consideration or estimate of the similarities or dissimilarities between two or more things.
5.example: Try to do a comparison between the two pie charts given for land use.

5.english_meaning: To a small or minor extent; slightly.
5.example: The land under forests has changed very marginally over the decades.

5.english_meaning: Lasting or intended to last or remain unchanged indefinitely.
5.example: The land under permanent pasture has decreased over time.

5.english_meaning: Land covered with grass and other low plants suitable for grazing animals.
5.example: Cows and goats depend on pasture land for grazing.

5.english_meaning: A result or effect of an action or condition.
5.example: What are the consequences of decreasing pasture land for our cattle?

5.english_meaning: Farmland that is plowed and harrowed but left unsown for a period in order to restore its fertility.
5.hindi_meaning: परती भूमि (वह कृषि भूमि जिसे कुछ समय के लिए खाली छोड़ दिया जाता है)
5.example: Most of the current fallow lands are cultivated once or twice.

6.english_meaning: The outer edge or border of something, such as a forest or area.
6.hindi_meaning: किनारा या सीमा (जैसे जंगल का बाहरी भाग)
6.example: Communities living on the fringes of these forests depend upon forest resources.

6.english_meaning: Having little or no rain; too dry or barren to support vegetation.
6.hindi_meaning: शुष्क या बंजर (जहाँ बहुत कम वर्षा होती है)
6.example: Waste land includes rocky, arid and desert areas.

6.english_meaning: The process in which the quality of something, especially land or environment, is lowered or damaged.
6.example: Continuous use of land without conservation measures has resulted in severe land degradation.

6.english_meaning: An unintended consequence occurring some time after an event or action, usually an unwelcome one.
6.example: Environmental damage has serious repercussions on society.

6.english_meaning: Made a problem, injury, or offense worse or more severe.
6.hindi_meaning: और अधिक गंभीर करना या बढ़ाना
6.example: Human activities have aggravated the pace of natural forces to cause damage to land.

6.english_meaning: The clearing of a wide area of trees and forests.
6.example: Deforestation due to mining has caused severe land degradation in several states.

6.english_meaning: Extracting stone or other materials from a quarry or open pit.
6.hindi_meaning: उत्खनन या खदान से पत्थर निकालना
6.example: Mining and quarrying contribute significantly to land degradation.

6.english_meaning: The concentration of salt dissolved in water or soil.
6.example: Over-irrigation leads to water logging, resulting in an increase in salinity in the soil.

6.english_meaning: Liquid waste or sewage discharged into a river or the sea from an industrial plant.
6.example: Industrial effluents have become a major source of land and water pollution.

6.english_meaning: The establishment of a forest or stand of trees in an area where there was no previous tree cover.
6.example: Afforestation and proper management of grazing can help solve land degradation.

6.english_meaning: Rows of trees or shrubs planted to protect an area from wind and soil erosion.
6.hindi_meaning: रक्षक मेखला (हवा से बचाने के लिए पेड़ों की कतारें)
6.example: Planting of shelter belts helps check land degradation in arid areas.

6.english_meaning: The action of making something stable, firm, or less prone to shifting.
6.example: Stabilisation of sand dunes can be achieved by growing thorny bushes.

6.english_meaning: The process by which water on the ground surface enters the soil.
6.hindi_meaning: अंतःस्यंदन (पानी का मिट्टी के अंदर रिसना)
6.example: Dust settling on land retards the process of infiltration of water into the soil.

6.english_meaning: The physical features and elevations of an area of land.
6.example: Relief, climate, and parent rock are important factors in soil formation.

6.english_meaning: Changed in color or form over time due to exposure to the weather or natural elements.
6.example: The subsoil consists of weathered rocks, sand, silt, and clay.

7.english_meaning: Made up of sand, silt, and clay left behind by running water.
7.hindi_meaning: जलोढ़ (नदियो द्वारा बहाकर लाई गई मिट्टी से बना)
7.example: The northern plains of India are formed by fertile alluvial soil.

7.english_meaning: Old alluvial soil found further away from the river, containing higher concentrations of kankar nodules.
7.example: The bangar soil contains a higher concentration of kankar nodules compared to the khadar.

7.english_meaning: New alluvial soil found in floodplains with finer particles and higher fertility.
7.example: Khadar is more fertile than bangar because it gets renewed every year during floods.

7.english_meaning: Lying or formed at the base of a mountain or mountain range.
7.hindi_meaning: पर्वतपदीय (पहाड़ के तलहटी या आधार पर स्थित)
7.example: Coarse soils are more common in piedmont plains such as Duars and Chos.

7.english_meaning: Another name for black soil, which is ideal for growing cotton.
7.example: Black soils are also known as regur soils and are excellent for cotton cultivation.

7.english_meaning: A dark, fine-grained volcanic rock formed from lava flows.
7.hindi_meaning: बेसाल्ट (ज्वालामुखी के लावा से बनी एक चट्टान)
7.example: The Deccan trap region is primarily made up of basalt rock.

7.english_meaning: Derived from living matter or plants and animals.
7.example: Soil consists of both organic matter like humus and inorganic materials.

7.english_meaning: Not consisting of or coming from living matter; mineral-based.
7.hindi_meaning: अजैविक (निर्जीव या खनिज पदार्थों से संबंधित)
7.example: Inorganic materials in the soil include various mineral particles.

7.english_meaning: Having a pH greater than 7; basic rather than acidic.
7.hindi_meaning: क्षारीय (जिसमें क्षार की मात्रा अधिक हो)
7.example: Soils in drier areas tend to be more alkaline and require proper treatment.

7.english_meaning: Prepared and used for growing crops.
7.example: Due to high fertility, regions of alluvial soils are intensively cultivated.

7.english_meaning: The feel, appearance, or consistency of a surface or substance, such as the size of soil particles.
7.hindi_meaning: बनावट या गठन (मिट्टी के कणों का आकार)
7.example: The soil texture varies from sandy to clayey across different regions.

7.english_meaning: Water or other liquid diffused in a small quantity as vapour, or condensed on a surface.
7.example: Black soils are well-known for their high capacity to hold moisture.

7.english_meaning: Substances that provide nourishment essential for the growth and maintenance of life.
7.example: Black soils are rich in essential soil nutrients such as calcium and potash.

7.english_meaning: The arrangement of the natural physical features of an area.
7.example: The varied relief features and topography of India influence soil formation.

7.english_meaning: In a way that concentrates a great deal of effort, resource, or activity on a single subject or place.
7.hindi_meaning: सघन रूप से या बड़े पैमाने पर
7.example: The fertile river plains are intensively farmed to feed the large population.

8.english_meaning: Belonging to or occurring in the present time.
8.example: Contemporary India focuses on sustainable development and modern challenges.

8.english_meaning: The upper layer of earth in which plants grow, a black or dark brown material typically consisting of a mixture of organic remains, clay, and rock particles.
8.example: Alluvial soil is one of the most fertile soil types found in India.

8.english_meaning: Categories of things or people having common features.
8.example: There are several major soil types found across the Indian subcontinent.

8.english_meaning: Important, serious, or significant in size, amount, or extent.
8.example: Agriculture is a major economic activity in rural India.

8.english_meaning: A country in South Asia, occupying the greater part of the Indian subcontinent.
8.example: India has diverse geographical features and climatic zones.

8.english_meaning: An edition of a work printed from existing type without alteration, often for new academic sessions.
8.example: This textbook is a government reprint for the academic year.

8.english_meaning: The study of the physical features of the earth and its atmosphere.
8.example: Geography helps us understand the relationship between people and their environments.
